chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When a woman kills a man, she is executed for it; and when a man kills a woman, if retaliation is intended, they pay the remainder of the man's wergild and retaliate him with it; and if they do not do so if they do not do it, they accept from the killer the wergild of the woman in full, and the wergild of the woman is half the wergild of the man.

key_terms.قَوَد: Retaliation (execution of the killer in kind)
key_terms.نِصْفُ دِيَةِ الرَّجُلِ: Half the wergild of the man

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in blood money and retaliation when a man kills a woman versus a woman kills a man?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudential nuance of qisas (retaliation) and diyah (blood money) when gender differences exist between the killer and the victim, reflecting the Shia view that a woman's life is not directly equivalent to a man's in terms of execution cost. It highlights the heirs' discretionary choice to either pay the differential amount to execute the male killer or accept the full female diyah as compensation, thereby preserving the principle of proportional justice. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for understanding the economic and legal valuation of life in homicide cases.
